title: Airtable Not Syncing or Updating: How to Fix It
body_md:
![support.airtable.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/airtable-not-syncing-or-updating-how-to-fix-it/1.png)
*Screenshot of support.airtable.com ([source](https://support.airtable.com/docs/troubleshooting-syncs-in-airtable))*

If a table synced from another Airtable base shows a warning icon, its sync may need re-authentication. Create a fresh syncable view share link at the source, then use **Update sync configuration** in the destination. For a sync from an integrated service such as Google Drive, reconnect the source account instead. See [Airtable's sync troubleshooting](https://support.airtable.com/docs/troubleshooting-syncs-in-airtable).

If there's no error icon and the table just looks stale, keep reading — that's a different problem with a different fix.

## Why This Happens

![support.airtable.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/airtable-not-syncing-or-updating-how-to-fix-it/2.png)
*Screenshot of support.airtable.com ([source](https://support.airtable.com/articles/2849803278-getting-started-with-airtable-sync))*

Airtable sync pulls data from a source view into a destination table. It can be configured one-way, two-way, or as a multi-source sync that brings several sources into one table. It breaks in a handful of predictable ways:

- **The share link changed at the source.** Once a syncable view share link is regenerated, every synced table sourcing from that view stops syncing until the destination sync is reconfigured. One person "cleaning up" share links can break every downstream table.
- **Nobody's been in the destination base.** Automatic syncs can stop running on a destination base that hasn't had recent activity, which looks exactly like a table that "hasn't updated in a while" even though the source is fine.
- **The source itself changed.** The share link may have been removed or regenerated, or its settings modified; for sync integrations, the source dataset may have been deleted or changed, or the connected account may no longer be valid.
- **The person who set up the sync is gone.** Syncs are tied to the collaborator who configured them — if that user is removed from the destination base, the connection breaks and stops updating, and Airtable calls this expected behavior.
- **Permissions or plan limits.** Airtable respects password and email domain restrictions on view share links. Sync is also plan-dependent: workspaces on the free plan don't get the automatic sync option at all.
- **The sync is just slow.** Large source views can take a while on the first pull.
- **The base is overloaded.** If external integrations hit a base with requests around the clock, the request queue can get backed up, making tables slow to load for human users.

## Step-by-Step Fixes

![support.airtable.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/airtable-not-syncing-or-updating-how-to-fix-it/3.png)
*Screenshot of support.airtable.com ([source](https://support.airtable.com/docs/third-party-integrations-common-troubleshooting))*

### 1. Check for the error icon first

Open the destination base and look at the synced table's name. A visible error icon ⚠️ on the synced table is how Airtable says you identify a broken sync — and it means the sync likely needs re-authenticating. If a last-synced timestamp is shown, it tells you whether this started an hour ago or three weeks ago.

No icon? Skip to step 4.

One caveat before you touch anything: you need creator permissions in the base where you're configuring the sync, and editors can only set up the source share link, not the destination sync.

### 2. Re-authenticate with a fresh share link

At the source base, open the view being synced and create or copy a syncable view share link. Then in the destination base, click the dropdown next to the synced table name, click **Update sync configuration**, paste the link and save — the sync re-authenticates under your credentials and resumes.

Heads up: regenerating a share link affects every sync dependent on that source view, and each target has to be updated. Warn teammates before you do it in a shared workspace.

### 3. If the source is an external app, reconnect the account

For tables synced from Google Calendar, Jira, Salesforce, and similar integrations, the token is usually the culprit. Airtable's guidance for third-party integration errors starts with reconnecting the external account, and notes that some users have better luck removing the account entirely and re-adding it as a new connection. Rebuilding the component from scratch is the step after that.

### 4. Trigger a manual sync and wait a few minutes

If the table is simply stale, this is your fix. Open the synced table's dropdown and choose **Sync now** to pull the latest data, then restore regular activity in the destination base — scheduled automations or API updates count, as long as they change data in that base.

Give a big source view a few minutes before you call it broken.

### 5. Test whether it's one view or the whole sync

Try syncing a different view from the same source base. If a second view syncs fine, the problem is in the original view's configuration, filters, or field set — not your account or the base.

While you're in there, check the field mapping. Under 'Edit synced fields' you can see the current sync mapping, and toggling a field **On** and confirming it maps to the right destination field fixes fields that silently never arrive.

### 6. Rebuild the sync

If the sync still fails, create a new test synced table from the same source and compare it. Keep the original table until the test works and you've reviewed dependent fields, views and automations. Don't delete a working configuration just to experiment. Removing or reconnecting an external account can affect other automations that use it.

### 7. Clear cache, then check base performance

Clearing your browser's cache and cookies is a standard part of Airtable troubleshooting. If the whole base feels sluggish, trim the load: formula fields — especially time-based ones using NOW() — are taxing on large bases, so remove unnecessary formulas and use TODAY() instead of NOW() where the precision isn't needed.

Also remove unneeded lookups, rollups, and formulas that reference linked records.

### 8. Contact support with specifics

If the error persists across views and users, contact Airtable Support with the source base, table, and view names.

Include a screen recording hosted online (Loom, Zight, etc.) rather than an MP4 attachment or a Google Drive upload, which often blocks their team from viewing it.

Also tell them roughly how many rows the source has, whether the sync worked before, and when it last synced correctly.

## How to Prevent It Next Time

![support.airtable.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/airtable-not-syncing-or-updating-how-to-fix-it/4.png)
*Screenshot of support.airtable.com ([source](https://support.airtable.com/articles/2512153420-troubleshooting-airtable-base-performance))*

- **Don't regenerate source share links casually.** Treat them as production infrastructure and document which destinations depend on each one.
- **Keep an eye on quiet destination bases.** Airtable's own fix for dormant automatic syncs is regular activity in the base, which can come from automations or the API — so schedule something small if nobody opens the base.
- **Name the owner.** Airtable suggests setting a table description so collaborators know where the data comes from and who to contact if the sync breaks. Since syncs die with the collaborator who made them, that note matters more than it sounds.
- **Keep source views lean.** Fewer fields and filtered record sets sync faster.
- **Check status before you debug.** Airtable publishes a public status page; glance at it before tearing apart a working setup.

*Updated October 2026: this guide is written from Airtable's official documentation and public user reports, not from a controlled diagnostic test.*

## My Take

My read is that most "Airtable sync is broken" tickets aren't sync bugs at all — they're the dormant-base behavior. Airtable documents it plainly, but it's buried in a footnote about plan limitations, and it produces the most confusing possible symptom: no error, no warning icon, just old data sitting there looking current.

I think the second-biggest trap is that syncs belong to a person. Airtable ties the sync to whoever configured it, and removing that user from the destination base breaks the connection. If your sync was set up by a contractor or someone who's since changed teams, that's a dependency you should write down today rather than discover in a quarter-end report.

So the practical advice I'd give: before you touch anything, check whether an error icon exists. Icon means re-authentication. No icon means activity. Those two paths almost never overlap, and people waste hours regenerating share links — which breaks every other downstream table — for a problem that **Sync now** would have fixed.

To be fair to Airtable, real-time sync between bases that stay awake is genuinely reliable, and the dormancy rule is a defensible way to avoid burning compute on bases nobody opens. The complaint is about disclosure, not architecture.

I'm not a lawyer or a compliance professional, so if your synced tables feed anything with a regulatory or contractual deadline, treat a silent stale table as a real risk and build a freshness check into the destination base instead of trusting the sync to announce its own failure.
